mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 0.1% (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 6.5% signals labor market deterioration, triggering economic slowdown and negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances when UNRATE > 6.5% (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous FEDFUNDS < 0.1% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% signals accommodative policy amid inflation, driving positive equity returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Interaction condition occurs but 20-day returns are negative in >50% of cases (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) increase discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: Positive month-over-month HOUST growth indicates strengthening consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in >50% of instances when HOUST increases month-over-month (p-value > 0.05 for positive return rate).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production decline below 100 (base 2017=100) signals manufacturing contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances when INDPRO < 100 (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent positive GDPC1 growth and CPIAUCSL > 3.0% indicates robust economic expansion, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Interaction condition occurs but 20-day returns are negative in >50% of cases (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 6.0%) reduce consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of instances when UNRATE > 6.0% (p-value > 0.05 for negative return rate).
